meta.notes: Hebrew (Jewish) lunisolar calendar months with traditional associations. Holiday records are centralized in calendar-holidays.json.

calendar.label: Hebrew Calendar
calendar.description: The Hebrew calendar is a lunisolar calendar used for Jewish religious observances. The religious year begins with Nisan (month of Passover); the civil year begins with Tishrei. A leap year adds a second Adar (Adar II), making 13 months.

months.name: Nisan
months.description: The first month of the religious year. Called the 'month of redemption.' Passover (Pesach) commemorates the Exodus from Egypt.

months.name: Iyar
months.description: A month of counting and transition between Passover and Shavuot. Yom HaShoah and Yom Ha'atzmaut fall here.

months.name: Sivan
months.description: Month of the giving of the Torah at Sinai. Shavuot (Festival of Weeks) falls on the 6th.

months.name: Tammuz
months.description: A month associated with mourning. The Golden Calf was made and the Tablets were broken on the 17th.

months.name: Av
months.description: A month of mourning that ends with celebration. Tisha B'Av commemorates the destruction of both Temples.

months.name: Elul
months.description: A month of preparation and teshuva (repentance) before the High Holy Days. The shofar is blown daily.

months.name: Tishrei
months.description: The holiest month of the year. Contains Rosh Hashanah (New Year), Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement), and Sukkot.

months.name: Cheshvan
months.description: Also called Marcheshvan. The only month with no Jewish holidays. Day count varies between 29–30 in different years.

months.name: Kislev
months.description: Month of Hanukkah (Festival of Lights), which begins on the 25th. Day count varies 29–30.

months.name: Tevet
months.description: Hanukkah continues into the early days of Tevet. The 10th is a fast day marking the siege of Jerusalem.

months.name: Shvat
months.description: The month of Tu B'Shvat, the 'New Year for Trees.' Trees begin to wake in the Land of Israel.

months.name: Adar (Adar I)
months.description: A month of joy. Purim falls on the 14th. In a leap year this becomes Adar I and Purim is celebrated in Adar II.

months.name: Adar II
months.description: Added in a Hebrew leap year (7 times in every 19-year Metonic cycle). Purim is celebrated in Adar II in leap years.
